summary: On ChromeOS devices, autocomplete in the script editor can now be activated with Ctrl+Space.
extended_definition: On ChromeOS devices, autocomplete in the script editor can now be activated with Ctrl+Space.

supporting_pages.title: Google Apps Script release notes \_|\_ Google for Developers
evidence_snippets: Feature On ChromeOS devices, it is now possible to activate autocomplete (sometimes called "content assist") with the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Space .
Autocomplete in the editor has been enhanced to be faster, more consistent, and extends its support to user-defined functions and JavaScript language features.
Fixed Fixed some issues where autocomplete stopped working after certain statements were typed in the script editor.

supporting_pages.title: Google Sheets Macros \_|\_ Apps Script \_|\_ Google for Developers
evidence_snippets: Import functions as macros If there is already a script bound to a sheet, you can import a function in the script as a new macro and then assign it a keyboard shortcut.
Sheets also automatically updates the script project manifest , recording the name and keyboard shortcut assigned to the macro.

Alternatively, you can create macros within the Apps Script editor by following these steps: In the Sheets UI, select Extensions > Apps Script to open the script bound to the sheet in the Apps Script editor.
